title: camcraft-ui lib tests: STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION ends the test process at a random test (Windows 11)

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Main is broken or a regression with no workaround; blocks a cut

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
The `camcraft-ui` lib test binary often ends with `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION` (0xc0000005) on Windows. The crash is in the test process, not in one test. It makes `cargo xtask gate quick` red at the step `ui suites: lib` about half of the time.

## What happens
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` runs. The process stops with `process didn't exit successfully ... (exit code: 0xc0000005, STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION)`.
- No test shows FAILED. There is no panic message and no summary line. The last lines are `... ok` lines of different tests.
- The crash comes after 332 to 381 tests have finished (of 1479). The last test is different each time. Examples: `egui_app::tests::a_gated_dropdown_row_click_answers_and_closes`, `egui_app::status_alert::tests::ordinary_status_is_not_an_alert`, `egui_app::start_exit_rows::tests::a_typed_start_point_applies_through_the_history_and_undoes`, `egui_app::sinker_pass_tests::a_rough_op_shows_its_pass_and_the_finished_cavity_size`.

## How often
Debug profile (`cargo test`, unoptimized + debuginfo), default number of test threads (16):
- Plain `main` (commit 4c0a157e1): 8 of 15 runs crashed. The tests finished before the crash: 332, 354, 358, 361, 362, 369, 371, 371.
- A branch with a small, unrelated change (a worker thread for the stock eye): 2 of 10 runs crashed, after 366 and 381 tests.

## Conditions
- It is not tied to the job count of the gate. `cargo xtask gate quick` crashed with 16 jobs (`--test-threads=16`). It crashed once with `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=4` (`--test-threads=4`) and passed once with 4 jobs on a different branch.
- One test thread: 6 of 6 runs passed (1475 tests, about 3 minutes each, `main`). So the crash needs tests that run at the same time. This is a reading of 6 runs, not a proof.
- Windows 11 Home 10.0.26300, a laptop with 16 logical CPUs.
- GPU: Intel Arc B390 (integrated), driver 32.0.101.8628.
- Toolchain: rustc 1.99.1 (58cf8f9c3 2026-10-13), cargo 1.99.1, target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.

## Effect on the gate
- `ui suites: lib` is red in about half of the runs. A change that does not touch the cause cannot show a green lib step reliably.
- A pull request that needs the quick gate can show 1479 passed in one run and a crash in the next run on the same head.

## Stack trace
There is none. I tried for about one hour and did not change any CamCraft code.
- No debugger is installed here. Windows crash dumps need a registry change with administrator rights. I did not make it.
- I wrote a small program that starts the test binary with the Win32 debug API and prints the stacks of all threads at the first access violation. With the debugger attached, the test process ended on its own with exit code 0 or 101 after 70 to 119 tests, in every run, so it could not reproduce the crash. I think a debugger changes what the process does. I did not find why.

## Questions for the maintainers
1. Does the crash happen on your runner (`post-merge.yml`, Windows or other)? Do you know the cause?
2. While it exists, how do you want a pull request treated if `ui suites: lib` crashes but the pinning tests, run by name, pass? My plan is to name the crash in the PR body and to show the named tests.
3. Which setting should I use to get a crash dump (for example `LocalDumps` for `camcraft_ui-*.exe`), if you want one?

## A different observation, probably not related
With 16 jobs, the step `ui build (--no-run)` of `cargo xtask gate quick` failed in 4 of 4 runs with `found invalid metadata files` or `found possibly newer version of crate`. The crate was `png`, `accesskit`, `zerocopy` and `test` in different runs. `cargo clean -p camcraft-ui` did not help. With `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=4` the build step passed in both runs. I think it is a build-cache problem on this machine. I did not look further.
